Introduction: 
Accounting is the language of Business: Manufacturing and trading entities are important organs of the world’s economic dimension. The economic dimension of the world is often described as economy.
 In an economy, financial transactions are inherent.  Companies and other entities need to communicate to the employees and the public and statutory administrative bodies about the transactions they perform which have financial implications.  This need is precisely addressed by a language called accounting. Accounting framework is an important edifice like technical, legal and other entities.
Accounting is perhaps the single largest edifice of a business edifice with, and around, which the whole gamut of other edifices are built and intertwined. 
Accounting is very often the basis for decision making – both internal and external. Whether to increase prices or cut costs or “Buy, Sell or Hold” decisions, companies need to have their accounting systems in place. 
Course Design:
The Course on Advanced Topics in Accounting is designed with the following focus: 
1.        To enable students to understand certain advanced Accounting standards 
2.        To enable students to better appreciate the contents of financial statements – to be read along with other aspects of annual reports (like Chairman’s report / Board of Directors report) 
3.        To enable students to apply various management accounting tools used for decision making and control especially in the context of Strategic Cost Management
